stem:
Dipti chooses clothes for hot summer days and for cold winter days. She compares light-coloured and dark-coloured cloth in sunlight and notes that some shirts are thin and lightweight.

Which claims are correct? One or more options may be correct.

options.text: In summer, light-coloured clothes are better because they reflect more of the heat that falls on them.
In winter, dark-coloured clothes are better because they absorb more of the heat that falls on them.
In summer, dark-coloured clothes are better because they reflect more heat.
A thin lightweight dark-coloured shirt reflects more heat than a light-coloured shirt because it is lightweight.

teacher.key_rationale: Light colours mostly reflect incident heat; dark colours mostly absorb it. So light clothes suit summer and dark clothes suit winter. Reversing that mapping, or treating weight as the heat rule, is wrong.
